questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is rural development?

options.A: The planned process of improving the economic, social, institutional and environmental conditions of people living in rural areas
options.B: The process of shifting rural population to urban areas
options.C: The development of only agricultural production in villages
options.D: The construction of roads in rural areas only

questions.explanation: Rural development is the planned process of improving the economic, social, institutional and environmental conditions of people living in rural areas.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the central aim of rural development?

options.A: To increase urban migration
options.B: To improve the quality of life of rural people by reducing poverty, creating employment, strengthening agriculture and allied activities, and providing essential services and infrastructure

questions.explanation: The central aim is to improve the quality of life of rural people by reducing poverty, creating employment, strengthening agriculture and allied activities, and providing essential services and infrastructure.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Is rural development limited to agricultural development?

options.A: Yes, it deals only with agriculture
options.B: Yes, it deals only with irrigation
options.C: No, it includes agriculture, animal husbandry, fisheries, rural industries, education, health, housing, roads, drinking water, sanitation, skills, financial inclusion and local self-government

questions.explanation: Rural development is not limited to agriculture; it includes agriculture, animal husbandry, fisheries, rural industries, education, health, housing, roads, drinking water, sanitation, skills, financial inclusion and local self-government.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What are the major dimensions of rural development?

options.A: Economic development, social development, human development, infrastructure development, institutional development and environmental sustainability

questions.explanation: The major dimensions are economic development, social development, human development, infrastructure development, institutional development and environmental sustainability.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is inclusive rural development?

options.A: Development that benefits only large farmers
options.B: Development that ensures the benefits of development reach all sections, particularly women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities, landless labourers and other vulnerable groups
options.C: Development that benefits only urban residents

questions.explanation: Inclusive rural development ensures that the benefits of development reach all sections, particularly women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, persons with disabilities, landless labourers and other vulnerable groups.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is sustainable rural development?

options.A: Development that exhausts natural resources quickly
options.B: Development that improves present living conditions without exhausting natural resources or reducing the ability of future generations to meet their needs
options.D: Development that benefits only the present generation

questions.explanation: Sustainable rural development improves present living conditions without exhausting natural resources or reducing the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is rural poverty?

options.A: A condition in which individuals or households living in rural areas lack sufficient income and resources to meet basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, education and a dignified standard of living

questions.explanation: Rural poverty is a condition in which individuals or households living in rural areas lack sufficient income and resources to meet basic needs such as food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, education and a dignified standard of living.

questions.explanation: Rural poverty may be income poverty, multidimensional poverty, food and nutrition poverty, asset poverty, social exclusion and lack of access to essential public services.

questions.question: What is absolute poverty?
